content.value_statement: Poor schema choices create slow queries, fragile migrations, and inconsistent data. This skill guides SQL and NoSQL design with normalization, indexes, constraints, migrations, and review checklists.
actual_capabilities: Guides SQL normalization from first normal form through third normal form.
Compares SQL and NoSQL modeling choices for common application patterns.
Recommends indexes for foreign keys, filters, sorting, and composite queries.
Explains constraints, keys, relationship patterns, and data type selection.
Provides migration safety patterns for reversible and zero-downtime changes.
Includes a schema design checklist and a reusable migration template.
limitations: It does not connect to live databases or inspect production schemas automatically.
It does not execute migrations, benchmark queries, or validate engine-specific syntax.
It requires clear requirements, relationships, scale targets, and access patterns.
Examples may need adaptation for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, or other engines.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Application Schema
use_cases.description: Design entities, relationships, keys, constraints, and indexes before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Review a Migration Plan
use_cases.description: Check a proposed migration for rollback safety, compatibility, constraints, and deployment risk.

use_cases.title: Improve Slow Data Access
use_cases.description: Analyze query patterns and identify indexing, denormalization, and pagination improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner schema planning for a new product feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a database schema for this feature: [describe feature]. Include entities, relationships, primary keys, and important constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Choose SQL or NoSQL
prompt_templates.scenario: Select a database model before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare SQL and NoSQL options for this workload: [describe data, queries, scale, and consistency needs]. Recommend one approach and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Indexes and Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this schema description and access patterns: [paste summary]. Identify missing indexes, weak constraints, and risky data types.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced rollout planning for production schema changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reversible, low-risk migration plan for this change: [describe old schema, new schema, data volume, and deployment process]. Include validation and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: A marketplace needs users, products, orders, payments, and shipment tracking.
output: A normalized entity list with separate order, order item, payment, and shipment records.
Recommended foreign keys, uniqueness rules, timestamps, and indexes for common lookups.
Notes about order history, payment status changes, and audit requirements.

output_examples.input: A team wants to add a required customer phone field to a large users table.
output: A multi-step migration plan that starts with a nullable field and backfill phase.
Deployment guidance for writing both old and new fields during rollout.
Validation and rollback checks before enforcing the final required constraint.

output_examples.input: An analytics dashboard has slow filtered order queries by customer, status, and date.
output: A composite index recommendation based on the filter order and selectivity.
Suggestions to avoid broad row scans and unnecessary selected columns.
A reminder to verify the query plan after adding indexes.

best_practices: Provide expected queries and write patterns before asking for schema recommendations.
Ask for migration steps separately from the target schema design.
Review generated examples against the specific database engine and application framework.
anti_patterns: Do not request a schema using only screen names or user interface fields.
Do not copy example migrations into production without testing on realistic data.
Do not add every possible index without measuring write cost and storage impact.

faq.question: Does this skill support both SQL and NoSQL databases?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers relational normalization, document modeling, embedding, referencing, and indexing tradeoffs.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready migrations?
faq.answer: It can outline migration steps and templates, but engineers must adapt and test them before production use.

faq.question: Does it inspect my existing database automatically?
faq.answer: No. You must provide schema details, query patterns, constraints, and performance concerns.

faq.question: Can it help with zero-downtime changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains staged rollout patterns, backfills, compatibility, validation, and rollback planning.

faq.question: Is it useful for schema reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides checklist-based review for keys, constraints, indexes, migrations, and data integrity.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
